# Temple Scroll Column 31 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** 11QT (Cave 11), Col. 31 | **Condition:** well preserved

---

**31:1** On the eastern side, the outer court shall measure one thousand six hundred cubits, from one corner to the other.

**31:2** You shall construct three gates in it, spaced equally from each other and from the corners of the court.

**31:3** Each gate shall open toward the east, and they shall bear the names of the sons of Israel:

**31:4** Simeon, Levi, and Judah — these shall be the names of the eastern gates.

**31:5** On the northern side, by the same measurement: one thousand six hundred cubits.

**31:6** You shall construct three gates on the northern side, equally spaced from one another and from the corners.

**31:7** They shall bear the names of the sons of Israel: Reuben, Joseph, and Benjamin.

**31:8** These shall be the names of the northern gates.

**31:9** On the western side, you shall construct by the same measurement: one thousand six hundred cubits.

**31:10** You shall construct two gates on the western side, and they shall bear the names:

**31:11** Issachar and Zebulun — these shall be the names of the western gates.

**31:12** On the southern side, you shall measure by the same measurement: one thousand six hundred cubits.

**31:13** You shall construct three gates on the southern side, and they shall bear the names:

**31:14** Gad, Asher, and Naphtali — these shall be the names of the southern gates.

**31:15** The length of each side of the outer court shall be one thousand six hundred cubits, from corner to corner.

**31:16** There shall be twelve gates for the outer court, corresponding to the twelve tribes of Israel.

---

*LOGOS notes: Column 31 describes the outer court perimeter and assigns tribal names to its twelve gates. The arrangement echoes Ezekiel's vision but reflects the Qumran community's distinctive ideal. The western wall has only two gates, distinguishing this plan from a symmetrical twelve-gate arrangement.*
